title: UP Poet Laureate reads paranormal stories at Ishpeming Carnegie Library
excerpt: The poems and short story were written by Dr. Matherne herself and were inspired by her own love of gothic literature and a real paranormal encounter.
content:
ISHPEMING, Mich. (WLUC) - A special guest at Ishpeming Carnegie Library helped listeners get into the Halloween spirit with several spooky poems.

U.P. Poet Laureate Emerita Dr. Beverly Matherne read four of her own poems, as well as a short story at the library. The stories were paranormal themed to help keep with the Halloween season.

Dr. Matherne says one of her poems was based on a real paranormal encounter she had in the past. She also cites her New Orleans background as an influence on her work due to the area’s gothic background.

“There’s a whole history and tradition of gothic literature in the south,” Dr. Matherne said. “And I think that influences my writing because I had a steady diet of that as an English major down in Louisiana.”

Dr. Matherne says she is currently finishing up her new book on haikus.
